correctness.rationale: The exact one-point-extension game reduces at rank three to a centre with full adjacent and nonadjacent pairs. A seven-point witness must have three neighbours and three nonneighbours, and the precise within-part/cross-part degree conditions are necessary and sufficient. All 15 permutation cycle types and every subset of their induced 21-edge orbit sets are enumerated; their fixed point counts sum to 1,874,880, and division by 5,040 yields 372 orbits. Identity fixed graphs total 1,163,358, with independent exact edgewise coefficients. A separate original rank-recursion checker over 1,253 graph6 atlas representatives matches the entire unlabeled spectrum. The proof and C++17 source explain the complete finite orbit-cover, beyond a sampling experiment. Rank four would require at least 11 vertices, so all selected seven-point graphs have exactly rank three.

value.rationale: Seven is the proven natural first possible vertex order for rank three, not an arbitrary parameter choice. The complete spectrum by edge count and graph isomorphism refines the previously known unique minimum-edge witness to a full structural classification at the threshold, and supplies a precise labelled distribution for random minimal-order hosts. The rank-3 root rigidity and complement symmetry make the enumeration mathematically interpretable. This exact finite fact is not a known-table rerun: the ambient atlas has no rank filter, and the predecessor covered only the six-edge case. Future sharp forcing and minimal rank constructions can test against the now-classified first feasible layer.
